title: Constrained Subsequence Sum
description:
Given an integer array `nums` and an integer `k`, return the maximum sum of a **non-empty** subsequence of `nums` such that for every two consecutive elements `nums[i]` and `nums[j]` in the subsequence (with `i < j`), the index gap satisfies `j - i <= k`.

A subsequence of an array is obtained by deleting zero or more elements from the array while preserving the relative order of the remaining elements.
hints: Let `dp[i]` be the maximum constrained subsequence sum ending at index `i`. Then `dp[i] = nums[i] + max(0, max_{i-k <= j < i} dp[j])`.
Computing `max_{i-k <= j < i} dp[j]` directly takes `O(k)` per index, which is too slow when `k` is large.
Use a monotonic decreasing deque of indices `(j, dp[j])` over the sliding window `[i - k, i - 1]` to retrieve the maximum previous `dp` value in `O(1)` amortized time.

examples.explanation: Pick subsequence [10, 2, 5, 20] (indices 0, 1, 3, 4; all consecutive gaps <= 2), yielding 10 + 2 + 5 + 20 = 37.
The subsequence must be non-empty, so choosing the single largest element [-1] gives -1.
